title: Christ honored martyrdom by his own witness
english: For martyrdom is so wonderful and so much-sought-after that the Lord Jesus Christ himself, the Son of God, honored it by bearing witness to it, "not considering being equal with God something to be grasped" (Philippians 2:6), so that also with this gift he might crown the man into whom he descended.
orientation: Methodius opens his treatise by praising martyrdom, saying that the Lord Jesus Christ himself honored it by bearing witness to it.

added_allusions.reason: The clause not considering being equal with God something to be grasped quotes Philippians 2:6 (Greek ouch harpagmon hegesamenos to einai isa theo), and the published English already carries the citation (Philippians 2:6) inline, so only this added_allusions entry is new.

title: Beginning in human will, completion in God
english: Every good action has its beginning in our will, in which it has its substance, but its completion rests with God.
orientation: Methodius is closing the treatise by stating the principle that grounds his argument about martyrdom as a divine gift.
